text: Jean Galloway Bissell (June 9, 1936 – February 4, 1990) was a South Carolina attorney who advanced to a high-ranking position in banking and later served as a United States circuit judge on the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. Born in Due West, South Carolina, she obtained a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of South Carolina in 1956 and a Bachelor of Laws from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 1958. From 1958 to 1971, she practiced law in Greenville, South Carolina, and then continued in Columbia, South Carolina, until 1976. From 1976 to 1984, she served as an executive at South Carolina National Bank in Columbia, where she became the highest-ranking female executive among the 100 largest bank holding companies in the United States. During the 1970s and early 1980s, she also lectured at the University of South Carolina. On May 24, 1984, President Ronald Reagan nominated Bissell to a newly created seat on the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, established by 96 Stat. 25. This nomination followed Reagan’s earlier attempt in 1982 to appoint Sherman Unger, a United States Department of Commerce official, to the same seat, which failed due to significant opposition and Unger’s death from terminal cancer in late 1983. Bissell was confirmed by the United States Senate on June 8, 1984, and received her commission on June 11, 1984, becoming the first female South Carolina lawyer to serve as a federal judge. She served on the court until her death. Bissell died of cancer on February 4, 1990, at Sibley Memorial Hospital in Washington, D.C., at the age of 53.
